proposedOverrides.name: Ahé (Karipuna of Rondônia)
proposedOverrides.summary: Ahé, also known as the Karipuna of Rondônia, are a Tupi-Kawahib people of the Jacy-Paraná and Mutum-Paraná region in Brazil. Their communities continue despite devastating contact and territorial invasion.

identityAssessment.finding: The imported Ahé (Kawahib) polygon lies in Rondônia at about 64.96 to 64.29 degrees west and 10.29 to 9.58 degrees south. ISA and the 2023 field study identify Ahé as Karipuna of Rondônia. The imported Wikipedia Ahe match describes a Pacific atoll and is replaced. Neither the imported 1492 chronology nor exact geometry is verified by modern ethnography.

scopeNotes: ISA’s English and Portuguese accounts are one work for source-budget purposes. The new summary is included separately in the manual budget.
The 2022 recollections describe Adriano’s childhood and practice, not material remains excavated or dated to 1492. No archaeological attribution is invented.

The 2024 executive summary describes qualitative fieldwork from October to December 2023 by Rute Morais Souza and Melina Carlota Pereira, summarized by Arianne Rayis Lovo. Its residents count is not a total present-day ethnic population.
Older population estimates and the phrase four survivors describe different times and scopes; no current headcount is stated.
Historical use of the exonym Karipuna can be ambiguous. Eighteenth- and nineteenth-century travel descriptions are not automatically assigned to this Tupi-Kawahib community.
No medical efficacy claims, private ritual knowledge or precise locations of isolated people are added.
The Greenpeace report’s Maranhão training workshops are not attributed to the Karipuna. Its brief deforestation reduction is not presented as permanent success.
The 1998 legal recognition is not a founding date or verification of the imported polygon.
